title: High surface area microporous carbon materials for cryogenic hydrogen storage synthesized using new template-based and activation-based approaches
material_description: N-C-1 | unimodal microporous carbon (spherical particles); TEOS 2.08 g, sucrose 0.6 g; aerosol-assisted one-step template synthesis: TEOS pre-reacted in acidic ethanol/water, mixed with sucrose, atomized (TSI 3076, N2 carrier), particles condensed at 400 C, carbonized at 900 C (3 C/min) for 4 h under flowing N2; silica template removed with 10% HF
purification_method: silica template removed by soaking overnight in 10% HF; filtered, rinsed with water, dried at 100 C
source_location: main-05.png (journal p. 4), Table 1, row N-C-1, column "Hydrogen adsorption capacity (wt%)", footnote a
notes: Low-pressure H2 measured with Micromeritics ASAP 2010 (volumetric). Table 1 footnote a: "Measured at 77 K and 1.13 bars". Table 1 does not call the value excess (abstract: capacity "determined using excess hydrogen adsorption measurements at 77 K and up to 40 bar"), so uptake_type unspecified; basis_inferred excess by volumetric default. Table 1: total pore volume from analysis software at P/P0 > 0.97 (pore_volume_method other); micropore area and micropore volume method not stated; BET range not stated. Degassed at 120 C under vacuum for 12 h (end pressure not stated); "at least 100 mg" adsorbent per experiment (sample_mass_mg left empty); UHP-grade H2 and He used (no numeric purity); volumetric method with calibrated volumes, free-volume determination not described (calibration_described false).
measuring_lab_id: Meisner group, General Motors R&D Center
